fix.verify: Then push the change to the main branch and click “Re-verify” (or wait for the branch's automatic analysis).
fix.verify_dependency: Then regenerate the lockfile, push the change to the main branch and click “Re-verify” (or wait for the branch's automatic analysis).
fix.verify_image: Then rebuild and push the image with the same tag and click “Re-verify”.

no_fix.none_published: No fixed version of {{package}} has been published.
no_fix.check_usage: Check whether your code uses the vulnerable part (the advisory usually names the function or format).
no_fix.mitigate: If it does: mitigate (validate the input, disable the feature) or replace the dependency.
no_fix.accept: If it doesn't: record it as an accepted risk with its reason and a review date.

fix.manual_update: Update {{package}} to {{version}} or later in {{path}} and regenerate the lockfile.
fix.closes_all: Version {{version}} closes every advisory for {{package}} (this one only needs {{fixed}}).
fix.npm_transitive: {{package}} is a transitive dependency: force the version with “{{field}}” in package.json and reinstall.
fix.override_note: Better still: update the direct dependency that pulls it in.
fix.pip_line: In {{path}}, change the {{package}} line to “{{package}}>={{version}}” (or pin “=={{version}}”).
fix.go_stdlib: This is the Go standard library: build with Go {{version}} or later (update the build image and CI too).
fix.bundler_pin: If the Gemfile pins a version of {{package}}, raise it to “>= {{version}}”.
fix.maven_direct: Change the <version> of {{artifact}} in the pom.xml <dependencies>.
fix.maven_managed: Pin the version in the pom.xml dependencyManagement: that also applies it to the transitive dependency.
fix.gradle_constraint: Pin the version with a Gradle constraint (it works for transitive dependencies too).
fix.os_rebuild: This is an OS package in the image: the best fix is to rebuild it on an updated base image (docker build --pull).
fix.os_dockerfile: If the base image doesn't include the fix yet, upgrade the package in the Dockerfile:
fix.generic_update: Update {{package}} from {{installed}} to {{version}} or later in {{path}} and regenerate the lockfile.
fix.transitive_other: {{package}} comes in through another dependency: if the command doesn't upgrade it, update the direct dependency that pulls it in.
fix.malicious_sibling: {{package}} {{version}} is a malicious package: remove it instead of updating it (see its MAL- advisory). Updating isn't enough.

secret.revoke: Revoke or rotate the credential with its provider now: deleting it from the code isn't enough, it's already in the Git history.
secret.review_use: Check with the provider whether it was used from a source you don't recognize.
secret.vault: Move it to a secrets manager or an environment variable and read it from there.
secret.history: If the repository is or was public, consider rewriting the history (git filter-repo); rotating is what protects you.

fix_examples.py_eval_exec_non_literal: If you need operations, use a table of allowed functions instead of evaluating text.
fix_examples.py_shell_command_non_literal: Validate `name` against an allowlist or a strict pattern.
fix_examples.py_pickle_load: pickle runs code while deserializing: never use it on data you didn't produce yourself.
fix_examples.py_flask_debug_true: The Flask debugger lets anyone run code from the browser.
fix_examples.py_requests_verify_false: For an internal CA, pass its bundle: verify="/path/ca.pem".
fix_examples.py_weak_password_hash: For passwords: Argon2id, scrypt or bcrypt, never a fast hash.
fix_examples.py_ssrf_from_request: If the destination isn't fixed, resolve the name and reject private or metadata addresses.
fix_examples.js_command_injection: Validate `branch` against an allowlist or a strict pattern.
fix_examples.js_dom_xss_sink: If you need HTML, sanitize it with DOMPurify.
fix_examples.js_react_dangerously_set_inner_html: If you really need the HTML: DOMPurify.sanitize(comment) before inserting it.
fix_examples.js_jwt_hardcoded_secret: Rotate the secret that was in the code: it's already in the history.
fix_examples.java_objectinputstream_readobject: Better still: a data format (JSON) instead of Java serialization.
fix_examples.java_hardcoded_password: Rotate the password: it's already in the repository history.
fix_examples.php_command_injection: Better: validate $host against an allowlist first.
